newsitem.title: DENMARK: CARLSBERG SAYS STILL TALKING TO UTENOS.
newsitem.headline: CARLSBERG SAYS STILL TALKING TO UTENOS.

text.p: Danish brewer Carlsberg said on Wednesday that it was still in talks with Lithuanian beer-maker Utenos but declined to comment on a report that a Finnish-Norwegian suitor was seeking a stake in the firm.
"There is contact," Carlsberg spokesman Henrik Moelstroem told Reuters.
Lithuanian newspaper Verslo Zinios said Finnish-Norwegian joint venture Baltic Beverages Holding (BBH) sought 50 percent of Utenos Beverages and had offered 300 litas per share.
BBH is owned jointly by Finland's Hartwall and Pripps, part of Norway's Orkla .
BBH already owns most of another leading brewer Kalnapilis and if the company gets the 50 percent of Utenos it wants, it would control around 60 percent of the Lithuanian beer market.
Carlsberg has already said it wants to buy a controlling stake in Utenos, which is not quoted on the stock exchange.
Because of a disagreement with the government, which owns 21 percent of the company, Utenos has not yet succeeded in registering new shares with the securities commission.
The share capital of Utenos Beverages is currently 22 million litas. -- Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
